newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index gets new stocks on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index gets new stocks on Thursday.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index, which stormed to a record high on Wednesday, is set to get two new components on Thursday which could prompt an upward revision to year-end targets for the blue chip index, analysts said.
Red chip China Resources Enterprise Ltd and China-play Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings (CKI) will join the Hang Seng Index on Thursday.
They replace Oriental Press Group Ltd and Johnson Electric Holdings Ltd in the 33-stock index.
Simon Yeung, research manager at Lippo Securities, said the inclusion of China Resources, a sizable red chip, could be a reason to revise year-end targets for the Hang Seng Index.

The blue chip barometer stormed through 16,000 points for the first time ever on Wednesday, a year-end target for many brokerage firms, to a record high of 16,055.19 before finishing the day up 211.12 points at 15,983.18.

"Red chips are expected to have a good rally later this year on expectations of continued asset injection movements. With the inclusion of China Resources, some brokerage houses have already revised up their index targets," said Yeung.
Red chips are Hong Kong based companies with mainland Chinese financial backing.
China Resources and Cheung Kong Infrastructure have already benefited from the July 16 announcement by Hang Seng Index compiler HSI Services Ltd of their inclusion in the index.
CKI shares had risen 16.7 percent since mid-July to close at HK$26.90 on Wednesday and China Resources has gained 7.04 percent to finish at HK$38.00.
Analysts said CKI had benefited from buying by index funds while many had already bought China Resources shares before the news on expectations that it would be included.

Stanley Ng, research manager at Mansion House, said the inclusion of CKI and China Resource would boost the index's market representation since both companies had a larger market capitalisation than the stocks they were replacing.
But some brokers showed concern about CKI's relatively small free float of shares available in the market and its cross shareholding within the Cheung Kong group.

CKI, which has a 35.01 percent stake in Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd - also a Hang Seng Index component, is 84.58 percent owned by blue chip Hutchison Whampoa Ltd. Only about 15 percent of CKI shares are available to investors in the market.
Hutchison is in turn 48.95 percent owned by blue chip Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd.
HSI Services manager Tony Chiu said Hang Seng Index constituent stocks were reviewed on a quarterly basis, with the compiler looking at market capitalisation and trading volume.
"Cross holding and free floats are not factors considered currently," he said.
HSI has an advisory committee of nine independent professional members to review the Hang Seng Index stocks.
"We welcome comments from the market and we will take every comment and market response into consideration," Chiu said. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
